title: Inner child guide: headings for the narrow sidebar

scores.question:
Fable checked Opus's work of 16 November. Opus's pick holds up. Read by fresh readers for the first time, it sent them to the right section first on 53 to 55 of 68 situations, against 44 to 48 on your sidebar as it is today. GPT's and Fable's versions land in the same range, so choosing between them is about your voice, not about scores.

Each heading below now starts on Fable's pick: Opus's pick with 39 headings changed (12 of them only in their capitals) and one small heading added. Most changes keep more of your own words; five answer something the readers showed. Each changed heading says why. Anything you had already picked here is kept. Change any you like, or use a button; your answers save as you click. When you're done, tell me in the chat (or press Copy my answers and paste them there). Nothing goes into your post until you say so.

How sure I am: sure the renamed headings help readers find things (every renamed version beat your current sidebar with every reader). Not sure any one renamed version beats another.

68 situations: the 38 from 16 November and 30 new ones written by an agent that had seen only the guide's text, with no headings. The readers are AI models (Sonnet) who saw only one contents each, as the sidebar shows it. Fable's last two versions differ by one heading and still landed three apart, which is how much three readers can't tell. Two things no contents fixed: nobody looking for a real kind of gratitude found Ask God for a Loan (0 of 18; all went to The Joy In Sorrow), and for the voice that answers kindness with "I don't believe you", 3 of 18 reached a section that speaks to it.
